northstar-atlas-determinism.title: Northstar releases Atlas 1.0, staking simulation product on reproducible runs
northstar-atlas-determinism.dek: Privately held developer-tools firm says every run of its simulator can be replayed byte for byte.
body: SEATTLE - Northstar, a privately held developer-tools company, released version 1.0 of Atlas on Wednesday, a simulation runtime the company says can reproduce any recorded run exactly from its initial seed.

The product simulates processes, storage, networking and a browser inside a single deterministic environment. Northstar says the approach removes the wall clock, host randomness and unordered iteration from code running under the simulator, allowing failures to be replayed rather than reproduced by repetition.

Engineering manager Carol Nakamura said in an interview published by technology site The Verge that determinism 'does not make the software correct, it makes the incorrect parts stay still long enough to look at.' The Verge reported the release at http://theverge.com/2026/atlas-determinism
Northstar does not disclose revenue or headcount. The company said Atlas 1.0 is generally available and that its source is published at http://github.com/northstar/atlas

northstar-latency-incident.title: Northstar reports 12-minute API latency incident, no data loss
northstar-latency-incident.dek: Company publishes incident report the same day; customers report degraded response times.
body: Northstar said an incident on its public API caused elevated response times for approximately 12 minutes on Wednesday, and that no customer data was lost or exposed.
The company published an incident report at http://status.northstar.example/ and said a configuration rollback restored normal service. Northstar declined to say how many customers were affected.
